title: Heterogeneous backend timeline alignment and latency replay
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reconciliation and replay system that aligns and compares traces collected across heterogeneous tracing backends (Tempo, Jaeger, third-party vendors) so engineers can reason about end-to-end latency and symptom divergence. The service should detect clock skew and timestamp drift, normalize fields and tags, merge sampled and unsampled representations, and provide a replay harness to synthesize traffic that reproduces observed latency distributions for root-cause debugging.
updates: 2025-02-10 - Ticket created: proposal and goals captured; initial stakeholders: Observability, Runtime, Core Infra.
2025-02-14 - Prototype ingest adapter implemented for Jaeger v2 and Tempo HTTP collectors; synthetic test traces successfully forwarded to local reconciler (poC).

2025-02-17 - Decision: reconciliation will run as an eventual consistent pipeline (Kafka topic) rather than synchronous proxy to avoid adding latency to ingest path. Trade-off: slightly longer time-to-detect vs zero-impact on production ingest latency.

2025-02-19 - Added timestamp-correction module: uses per-host monotonic counters + median-based alignment across replicas to estimate clock skew. Initial results reduce inter-backend timestamp variance by ~22ms in lab traces.
2025-02-21 - Design review with PM/Design: console drilldowns will include a 'timeline alignment' view showing merged spans, detected skew, and per-backend delta bars. UX wireframes linked.

2025-02-25 - Integration tests added: cross-backend span-matching asserts (trace_id parity, consistent span names, tag normalization). Found mismatch pattern for instrumented SDK v1.3 where trace_id is hex vs base64; added normalizer rule.

2025-02-28 - Current blocker: vendor A sampling metadata is delivered in a proprietary header; need vendor contract to surface sampling flags or map them during ingestion. Tracking as dependency with Partner Eng.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciler accepts traces from at least 3 backend types (Tempo, Jaeger, vendor A) and emits a unified timeline for the same trace_id.
Clock skew detector flags hosts with >50ms drift and provides corrected timestamps; median alignment reduces inter-backend span timestamp variance to <10ms for synthetic tests.
Field normalization rules resolve common id mismatches (hex/base64 trace_id, tag name aliases) for >=95% of sampled traces in the test corpus.

Replay harness can ingest reconciled traces and generate synthetic traffic that reproduces the p50/p95/p99 latency distribution within +/-10% of the observed production window for validated workloads.
Console drilldown added with timeline overlay and per-backend deltas; linked dashboard panel and a debug Runbook for SREs.
Automated e2e tests added to CI that run against a local Tempo+Jaeger stack and fail the build if reconciliation accuracy drops below targets.
implementation_notes: Pipeline architecture: collector adapters -> kafka topic per-tenant -> reconciler workers -> normalized-output topic -> replay/historical store (parquet on s3).
Normalization steps: trace_id canonicalization, span_name alias mapping, status_code mapping, sampling_flag mapping (fall back to heuristics if header absent).
Clock skew detection: collect per-host monotonic counters, compute pairwise offsets and apply median correction per-trace before merge.
Matching strategy: primary key is trace_id; when absent, fall back to span signature (service+name+startWindowHash).
Replay harness: uses reconciled spans to issue synthetic requests to a local test-app; harness preserves inter-span gaps to emulate downstream queuing delays.
Testing: include deterministic fixtures for 5 canonical failure modes (clock drift, missing trace_id, id-encoding mismatch, sampling loss, timestamp truncation).
Perf targets: reconciler should sustain 10k traces/s per worker with <200ms processing latency under steady-state lab load.
